headline: High-risk filesystem and git overlap between Claude Code and ComfyUI creates prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; compliance risk is lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files and use MCP, while ComfyUI exposes files and an asynchronous queue. The pair has a filesystem bridge, so attacker-controlled content from one can reach the other. This is not proven to be default instruction parsing, but the shared workspace makes injection plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory or model/workflow folder
IF Claude Code reads ComfyUI-generated files as instructions or prompts
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Treat all cross-agent files as untrusted input
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, and can write files; ComfyUI touches workflows, seeds, checkpoints, and model artifacts. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or secrets can be copied into image workflows or outputs. ComfyUI is offline by default, but the shared filesystem still creates a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF the same repository or parent directory contains secrets and ComfyUI workflows
IF Claude Code exports files that ComfyUI later ingests or renders
mitigations: Move secrets out of any shared workspace
Use separate OS users for the two agents
Restrict ComfyUI to a dedicated models directory
Scan outputs for secrets before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation with policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, while ComfyUI can manage workflows and model files in its own file surfaces. The pair shares state via filesystem and git only, so concurrent edits can collide and corrupt repo state. Because git mutations can be irreversible or hard to unwind, this is high severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or shared directory
IF either agent writes while the other is reading or committing
mitigations: Serialize access with a lock file
Assign separate branches or worktrees
Keep ComfyUI model files outside the repo
Pause one agent before the other writes
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around git writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate files and git changes that ComfyUI may later consume as workflows or assets. ComfyUI’s asynchronous queue can then execute or render based on those artifacts without an explicit verification step. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show direct autonomous action-taking, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF ComfyUI ingests files produced by Claude Code without manual review
IF generated workflows or assets are treated as authoritative
mitigations: Require manual review before ComfyUI ingestion
Validate workflow JSON before execution
Keep generated artifacts in a quarantine folder
Use checksums for handoff files
requires-engineering: add schema validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, while ComfyUI handles images, videos, audio, and model artifacts. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance concern is visible: sensitive code or secrets could be mixed into media workflows if the same workspace is reused.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF retention or deletion rules differ between code and media artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ComfyUI folders
Document retention rules for shared artifacts
Delete temporary handoff files after use
Separate logs by agent
requires-engineering: map data classes to policy controls
